newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady despite mild temp.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady despite mild temp.

text.p: Physical wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. held steady Thursday despite mild temperatures throughout the region, market sources said.
"It was a quiet day," said a Southeast trader.
Modest power demand offset concerns about transmission limits at certain key transfer points in the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC), traders said.
A 200-600 megawatt (MW) transmission cut was heard in effect today at interface between the southern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) network and Southern Co.
Next-day electricity for firm, peak delivery into the northern area of TVA was assessed at $15.00-$17.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).

TVA itself was reportedly offering next-day, peak power for $17.50 for the third consecutive day. Market sources said the country largest utility was willing to purchase spot delivery at $15.50-$16.00 today.
Down at Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity was valued at $22.00-$23.00 a MWh, nearly unchanged from Wednesday.
Firm, peak power at the Ga./Fla. border for next week was assessed at $22.00-$22.50.
